text:
Lena: Heads-up — started getting a wave of p95/p99 spikes on /v1/chat around 14:02 UTC. Support opened several escalations; some logs show long token emission times and a few GPU OOMs.

Samir: saw the dashboard alert. Tail latency crept up from ~13:40 then jumped. Any infra or model rollouts?

Maya: no deploys in the window. Affected machines look to be Dedicated pool A, 40GB GPUs.

Carlos: do we have seq-length distribution? If sessions keep appending, KV cache growth can exhaust contiguous device memory and lead to fragmentation.

Lena: support traces indicate chats often start with 3–4k system+user tokens and then keep adding ~2k tokens. p99 rose ~4x. dmesg contains cuda OOM and allocator fragmentation warnings.

ops-bot: [ALERT] host-gpu-07 cuda alloc fails; mem_used=39.2GB/40GB

Samir: please grab nvidia-smi, allocator stats and KV metrics from a hot host. Also confirm CUDA version and whether cudaMallocAsync is used.

Maya: pulling logs from host-gpu-07. snippets: 

```
[14:03:52] failed allocation 2684354560 bytes, available 112589990
[14:03:53] runtime: KV entries: 1,450,213 total_kv=4.6GB avg=3.2KB
[14:03:53] cuda: falling back from cudaMallocAsync to cuMemAlloc
```

Maya: nvidia-smi shows a slow creep over several hours to ~98% usage.

Carlos: allocator fragmentation + large working set. What memory allocator are these workers built with?

Lena: tcmalloc in these images. For this customer we disabled eviction (--kv-eviction=false) to preserve history, so per-session KV kept growing.

Samir: likely cause. Short-term mitigations: 1) per-customer max_seq_len throttle, 2) trigger KV eviction or restart on affected workers, 3) steer traffic to larger-GPU spare pool.

Maya: executed soft eviction via admin API: `POST /admin/kv/evict?keep_last=64` — returned success but freed memory didn't immediately produce large contiguous free blocks; tcmalloc arenas still retained pages.

Carlos: tcmalloc tends to hold freed spans; jemalloc or aggressive release performs better. Also cudaMallocAsync behavior vs cuMemAlloc can affect fragmentation — we saw fallback to cuMemAlloc in logs.

Samir: immediate actions: 1) reroute the customer's traffic off pool A to pool B; 2) scale up pool B; 3) rolling graceful restarts of affected nodes to reset device allocators; 4) temporary session length cap (2048 tokens).

Lena: customer notified about soft 2k token cap; they acknowledged.

Maya: restarted 5 hosts in pool A with graceful drains. After restart, p95 on restarted nodes returned near baseline; first few requests had warmup latency.

Carlos: long-term items: expose allocator fragmentation metrics (retained bytes, arena count, kv_total_bytes); run jemalloc vs tcmalloc experiments; implement per-session KV upper bounds + LRU eviction; consider compression for older KV segments.

Samir: I'll add a burn-rate alert on kv_total_bytes and an automated steering play that shifts traffic when per-worker KV > 20% of GPU memory.

Maya: triage commands used: 

```
ssh host-gpu-07
sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "3 hours ago" | grep -E "failed alloc|KV entries|cuda"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
curl http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep kv_cache_bytes
```

Lena: we still had a few p99 reports after initial steering — autoscaler lag and some sticky sessions on old workers. Forced eviction + restart cleared the remaining nodes.

Maya: follow-up: added `--kv-max-bytes=8GB` per worker as a stopgap; on our canary it prevented recurrence for 24h but isn't a long-term solution.

Carlos: agreed. Also evaluate hybrid approach: in-place compression + LRU eviction for older context segments.

Samir: action items: Samir -> dashboard alerts & steering automation; Maya -> run jemalloc vs tcmalloc A/B test and record fragmentation metrics; Carlos -> design KV eviction algorithm with per-session/cost caps; Lena -> compile incident timeline, customer comms and postmortem. Sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

ops-bot: [INFO] rolling restart pool A completed 2026-03-14T14:27:18Z

Lena: closing note — recommend runbook step: if p95/p99 regresses and allocator OOM/alloc-failure logs show up, check KV growth and either evict or roll-restart. Set initial KV threshold at 20% of GPU mem for automated steering.
